title: The Vow of the Crescent Cove
premise: Dominic Quintana, a widowed single father running Crescent Cove's last bookshop, has spent ten years guarding a secret: the whirlwind romance he fled from in his twenties ended with a vow neither he nor the woman he loved ever spoke aloud. When a freak snowstorm traps his daughter's new teacher, Marisol Vega, in the shop with him — and Marisol turns out to be the woman he abandoned — the past arrives with a suitcase and an inheritance letter: her late grandmother left them both the cove's crumbling seaside cottage, but only if they claim it together within thirty days. Forced to renovate side by side, Dominic and Marisol must finally say the sentence they've rehearsed for a decade — 'I choose you' — before the deadline, the town's meddling, and his daughter's fragile heart make the choice for them. They claim the cottage, and each other, on the last possible night.
about_author: Wren Underhill is the pen name of a former lighthouse keeper's assistant who writes love stories set in small coastal towns where everyone knows your business. She lives in a drafty cottage with an opinionated cat and a shelf of romances she claims are 'for research.'

chapters.title: The Storm Makes the Guest List
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Closing the bookshop ahead of a sudden blizzard, Dominic is startled when new schoolteacher Marisol Vega takes shelter inside — and the recognition between them is instant and electric. He hides his panic behind tea and small talk while his daughter's drawing of 'Miss Vega' flutters on the counter. Beat: dread disguised as hospitality.

chapters.title: Ten Years, One Sentence
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Snowbound overnight, Marisol replays the summer in Lisbon when Dominic vanished without goodbye, and the vow they made to return to Crescent Cove together. She came to this town deliberately, carrying her grandmother's letter. She says nothing. Beat: resentment braided with unfinished love.

chapters.title: A Cottage with Two Names on It
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Marisol reveals the inheritance: her grandmother left the derelict cottage on the cove jointly to them both — conditional on joint restoration within thirty days. Dominic's carefully walled life cracks; his daughter Lila, delighted by Miss Vega, unknowingly tightens the trap. Beat: cornered by fate and fondness.

chapters.title: Terms of Renovation
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. They negotiate a coldly professional agreement — she handles the cottage, he keeps the shop, minimal contact — which the town immediately dismantles with gossip, casseroles, and unsolicited matchmaking. A leaked rumor of their history reaches Lila's school. Beat: the town as a benevolent antagonist.

chapters.title: What the Walls Remember
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Stripping wallpaper in the cottage, they uncover his late wife's childhood graffiti and, beneath it, the initials D+M carved a decade ago. Old grief and old love collide; Dominic admits, obliquely, why he fled — fear of not being enough. Beat: confession by plaster dust, almost.

chapters.title: The Deadline and the Daughter
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. With two weeks left, Lila asks Marisol if she's 'going to be the next mom,' forcing Marisol to confront that loving Dominic means risking Lila's heart too. Her grandmother's letter reveals the vow was the grandmother's own idea — a test of courage. Beat: stakes shift from romance to family.

chapters.title: Rival at the Door
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Marisol's polished ex-fiancé arrives with a counteroffer: buy out Dominic's half, sweep her away to the city. Dominic, stung into silence, lets him linger — and watches Marisol nearly say yes. Beat: the mistake of his twenties threatening to repeat as his thirties'.

chapters.title: The Night the Roof Gave
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. A storm collapses part of the cottage roof; Dominic arrives unasked and they shelter under tarpaulins, soaked and laughing, and finally speak the whole truth — his cowardice, her anger, the vow they both kept out of pride. They almost kiss; Lila calls, and the moment breaks. Beat: climax deferred, tension at breaking point.

chapters.title: Thirty Days, Last Night
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Deadline day. The cottage passes inspection, but the lawyer reveals the co-ownership can be dissolved — one signature and Marisol can walk free. Dominic chooses the sentence over the safety: in front of the whole town at the cottage door, he says 'I choose you,' and asks her to stay not for the house but for them. Beat: climax — the rehearsed sentence finally spoken.

chapters.title: The Vow of the Crescent Cove
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Epilogue in spring: the cottage restored, its new plaque reading 'Two Names, One Cove.' Marisol answers his vow with her own, Lila paints their initials beside the old carved ones, and the bookshop window displays a single book — her grandmother's letter, framed. Beat: resolution; loyalty and truth reconciled, home redefined.
